problem: Prove 'A|(B&C) |- (A|B)&(A|C)' using the analytical tableau method. Only one final answer, surrounded by <proof>...</proof>, using the notation described.
solution: We assume the premise A | (B & C) is true and the conclusion (A | B) & (A | C) is false. Expanding the falsity of the conjunction gives two branches: either A | B is false or A | C is false. In the branch where A | B is false, we derive A false and B false. From the premise A | (B & C), either A is true or B & C is true. But A true contradicts A false, and B & C true implies B true, which contradicts B false. So that branch closes. In the branch where A | C is false, we derive A false and C false. From the premise A | (B & C), either A is true or B & C is true. But A true contradicts A false, and B & C true implies C true, which contradicts C false. So that branch also closes. Since all branches close, the tableau is closed and the formula is valid.
